text:
“The last night we spent together,

asked:

—How many stars are there in the sky?

—Three hundred and fifty thousand.

—Bet you can't.

—Bet I can.


—Be quiet. Tonight

I do not want you asking such things.

Tonight, if you want to ask

how many stars there are in the sky,

or anything else,

ask something like: Do you love me?

Are you cold? Who says they are hungry?


Tonight, ask something that can be

answered in the wordless world.

Question with all your blood

something in which all the world's life

is asking,

something like: Who is crying?

Is anything needed?


And you will see how everything is needed,

and you will know how many stars there are in the sky

when you know that the sky has a single star

for each moment,

because if one is lost,

the light of the Universe will take one step into shadow.”

translation.title: How Many Stars Are in the Sky?
translation.editorial_note: The source begins with a stray closing quotation mark and ends with an opening one; the English repairs the enclosing punctuation while documenting the source anomaly.
